case_name: Keshav Chandra Joshi and Others v Union of India and Others
facts: The vexed question of inter se seniority between promotees and direct recruits has once again been brought to the force at the behest of the petitioners in these writ petitions filed u/art. 32...

The Governor of U.P. exercising the power under the proviso to Art. 309 of the Constitution of India, 1950 issued the U.P. Forest Service Rules, 1952, for short 'the rules' which became effective from January 2, 1952.
Rule 4 constitutes and fixes the cadre strength of Chief Conservator of Forest; Conservator of Forest; Deputy Conservator of Forest and Assistant Conservator of Forest.
The selection to the posts of Assistant Conservator of Forest was made but was ultimately vacated by this Court in A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India 1969 Indlaw SC 271
In May, 1966, the selection to the posts of Assistant Conservator of Forest was made but was ultimately vacated by this Court in A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India 1969 Indlaw SC 271
The process of recruitment was again started in the year 1972 but was stayed by the High Court of Allahabad in W.P. No. 119 of 1972.
With effect from May 1, 1975, the ratio of 25 per cent recruitment of promotees in Rule 6 was increased to 33 1/3 per cent.
issues: The legal questions or points of law being debated
No direct recruitment under Rule 5(a) till 1974 and even thereafter, promotees were appointed, admittedly on ad hoc basis, between March 13, 1974 and November 21, 1981, subject to direct recruitment
The service rendered from the dates of initial promotion till date of the substantive appointment should be treated as fortuitous
petitioner_arguments: The contention of Mr Mukhoty and Mr Garg, their learned senior counsel is that though the promotees were appointed on ad hoc basis due to non-availability of direct recruits to the vacant posts of Assistant Conservator or Forest, they are continuing for well over 5 to 12 years discharging the same duties, drawing the same scale of pay without any reversion.
The entire continuous length of service from the dates of their initial promotion should be counted towards their seniority

They strongly relied on Narender Chadha v. Union of India, 1986 Indlaw SC 661, Baleshwar Dass v. State of U.P., 1980 Indlaw SC 174, N.K. Chauhan v. State of Gujarat 1976 Indlaw SC 204 and proposition 'B' in Direct Recruits Class II Engineering Officers' Association v. State of Maharashtra, 1990 Indlaw SC 692
respondent_arguments: Their appointments, not being on the basis of merit as per rules, did not confer any right to the posts
Their seniority has to be counted only from the dates of substantive appointment

The delay to make direct recruitment had been occasioned only on account of the pendency of the proceedings right from Kraipak case 1969 Indlaw SC 271 in Allahabad High Court till the present group of writ petitions.

Since promotees were appointed in excess of the prescribed quota in Rule 6, they should be pushed down to the vacancies that had arisen in each year above the direct recruits as per the ratio as the promotees are not entitled to claim seniority from the initial dates of their respective promotions.
court_reasoning: The rules shall not apply to the members of the Indian Forest Service.
To accord just solution to this, we have set out only the relevant rules.

Rule 3(h) defines 'Members of the Service' to mean a person appointed in a substantive capacity under provisions of these rules or of rules or orders in force previous to the introduction of these rules, to a post in the cadre of the service'.
The above percentage will be observed if suitable officers are available for promotion to that extent.
holding: The petitioners claiming seniority over them filed the writ petitions seeking inter alia for the issue of: (a) a writ of mandamus to declare Rule 3(h) and Rule 24 of the Rules relating to reckoning of seniority from the date of the substantive appointment as illegal and violative of Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India, 1950;
The service rendered from the dates of initial promotion till date of the substantive appointment should be treated as fortuitous.

Since promotees were appointed in excess of the prescribed quota in Rule 6, they should be pushed down to the vacancies that had arisen in each year above the direct recruits as per the ratio as the promotees are not entitled to claim seniority from the initial dates of their respective promotions.
